steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Point: Punctuation is essential for AO6 (Technical Accuracy). Errors cost marks, but correct and sophisticated use can lift your writing to higher levels. Punctuation isn't just rules - it's about communication and effect. | Effect: Short sentences ending with full stops create a sense of finality, certainty, or drama. Each full stop is a pause, a breath, a moment of emphasis. | Comma Splice Error: Never join two complete sentences with just a comma. This is one of the most common punctuation errors in exams. Wrong: The door opened, she walked in. Right: The door opened. She walked in. Right: The door opened, and she walked in. | Semi-Colon vs Full Stop: A semi-colon suggests a closer connection than a full stop. Use it when you want to show that two sentences are thematically linked.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Add the missing punctuation: "the door opened she walked in slowly and looked around" | What's the difference between these two sentences? "The students' books" vs "The student's books" | When would you use a colon instead of a full stop?
